Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And by the night when it is still﴾ — he says: "and by the night when it comes."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, concerning God's words: ﴿And by the night when it is still﴾ — he said: "when people are clothed (in it), when it comes."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: when it departs.

Those who said that:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And by the night when it is still﴾ — he says: "when it departs."

Others said: its meaning is: when it becomes level and calm.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us; and Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, both from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And by the night when it is still﴾ — he said: "when it becomes level."

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And by the night when it is still﴾ — he said: "when it becomes level."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And by the night when it is still﴾ — "it became still with its creatures."

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿And by the night when it is still﴾ — he means: its settling and its stillness.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed me, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And by the night when it is still﴾ — he said: "when it becomes calm; that is its sajw (stillness), just as the stillness of the sea is its sajw."

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said its meaning is: "and by the night when it becomes calm with its people, and settles with its darkness," just as it is said: "a sajj sea" when it is still. From this is the saying of al-A'sha of Banu Tha'laba:

"So what is our fault if the sea of your cousin's sons surges,
while your sea is still (sajin), concealing nothing of the foam."

[Note: this verse appears in the commentary on Surah Al 'Imran 121 and Surah al-Qasas 88. Sibawayh 1:17; al-Khizanah 1:486. It is among the fifty verses of Sibawayh whose speaker is unknown. Al-Shantamari said: "He meant min dhanb, so he dropped the preposition and connected the verb, putting it in the accusative." Dhanb here is a collective noun. Therefore he said "you cannot count it." The wajh means aim and intention, and it means direction.]

And the saying of the rajaz poet:

"How good is the moonlit night, and the sajj night,
and tracks like the cloth of the weaver's woven sheets."

[The verse is not in his diwan. Some lines of the poem appear in it: 23 (printed edition of Muhammad Jamal), and al-Mujtana of Ibn Duraid: 23, describing a horse. Al-'Ir: the wild ass. Al-Hadr: fierce running; the wild ass runs fiercely. Al-Wana: fatigue and lethargy in running or work. Al-Ash'ab: a gazelle whose horns have split and separated greatly. The gazelle, when it grows old and its horns get grooves, is called nabh (Al-Hayawan 1:349). He describes his horse's intense speed, catching the wild ass that is confident in its speed, and the firm swift gazelle, hunting them before fatigue reaches it.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾

This is the answer to the oath, and its meaning is: "O Muhammad, your Lord has not abandoned you, nor has He hated you." It has also been said: "and nor has He detested (qala)," meaning: "nor has He detested you," relying on the listener's understanding of its meaning, since His saying "has not forsaken you" came before it, so it was known that the one addressed is the Prophet of God (ﷺ).

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ — he says: "your Lord has not left you, nor has He hated you."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ — he said: "your Lord has not detested you, nor hated you"; he said: "al-qali means the one who hates."

It has been mentioned that this surah was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) as a refutation by God of the Quraysh in their saying to the Messenger of God, when the revelation was delayed for him: "Muhammad's Lord has forsaken him and detested him."

Transmission of that report:

'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Dahhan narrated to me, saying: Mufaddal ibn Salih narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays al-'Abdi, from Ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: When Gabriel was delayed from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), a woman from his household, or from his people, said: "Satan has forsaken Muhammad." So God revealed to him: ﴿By the morning brightness﴾ ... to His words: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: Ibn 'Abd Allah is Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali.

Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Damghani and Muhammad ibn Harun al-Qattan narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, who heard Jundub al-Bajali say: Gabriel was delayed from the Prophet (ﷺ) until the polytheists said: "Muhammad's Lord has forsaken him." So God revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness and the night when it is still; your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, that he heard Jundub al-Bajali say: A woman said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "I do not see your companion except that he has delayed from you." So this verse was revealed: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, who said: I heard Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah say: A woman came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I do not see your devil except that he has left you." So it was revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness and the night when it is still; your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

Ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Shaybani narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, that Khadijah said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "I do not see your Lord except that He has detested you." So God revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness and the night when it is still; your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ — he said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, was delayed in bringing him the revelation, so some people, who were then in Makkah, said: "We do not see your companion except that he has detested you and forsaken you." So God revealed what you hear: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ — he said: Gabriel was delayed for him, so the polytheists said: "His Lord has detested him and forsaken him," so God revealed: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ — Gabriel remained away from Muhammad (ﷺ), so the polytheists said: "His Lord has forsaken him and detested him," so God revealed this verse.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ — he said: When the Qur'an was revealed to him, Gabriel was delayed from him for days, so he was reproached for that, and the polytheists said: "His Lord has forsaken him and detested him," so God revealed: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾.

Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, who said: Gabriel was delayed from the Prophet (ﷺ), so he became extremely distressed, and Khadijah said: "I see your Lord has detested you, because of what we see of your distress." He said: So this was revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness and the night when it is still; your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ ... to its end.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: the abode of the Hereafter, and what God has prepared for you in it, is better for you than the worldly abode and what is in it. That is: do not grieve over what has escaped you of it, for what you have with God is better for you than it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And your Lord will surely give you, O Muhammad, in the Hereafter of His abundant bounties, until you are satisfied.

The people of knowledge differed about what He promised him of giving. Some of them said: it is what

Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Awza'i narrate, from Isma'il ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi al-Muhajir al-Makhzumi, from 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was shown what would be opened to his community after him, town by town, and he was delighted by that. So God revealed: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾, and He gave him in Paradise a thousand palaces, in each palace what is fitting of wives and servants.

Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to me, saying: Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to me, from al-Awza'i, from Isma'il ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ — he said: a thousand palaces of pearl, whose dust is musk, and in them what suits them.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ — and that is on the Day of Resurrection.

Others said regarding that:

'Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ — he said: From the satisfaction of Muhammad (ﷺ) is that no one from his household enters the Fire.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, enumerates to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) His blessings upon him, and reminds him of His favors toward him: Did your Lord not find you, O Muhammad, an orphan and give you refuge? That is: He made for you a shelter to which you could resort, and a dwelling in which you could dwell. ﴿And He found you lost and guided you﴾ — He found you upon other than what you are upon today.

al-Suddi said concerning that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And found you lost﴾ — he said: He was upon the affair of his people for forty years. It has also been said: what is meant by that is: "He found you among a misguided people and guided you."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And found you poor and made you self-sufficient﴾

He says: He found you poor and made you self-sufficient. It is said of this: "so-and-so 'alah ya'il 'ailah," which means he became poor. From this is the saying of the poet:

"The poor man does not know when his wealth will come,
and the rich man does not know when he will become poor."

[Diwan: 507, praising Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik. al-Mawarid is the plural of mawrida, meaning the paths to water. He means the paths that people follow to reach their aims and needs, just as they follow watering routes to water.]

That is: when he becomes poor.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And found you poor﴾ — "poor."

It is mentioned that in the codex of 'Abd Allah it reads: ﴿And found you destitute, and gave refuge﴾.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge? And find you lost and guide you? And find you poor and make you self-sufficient?﴾ — he said: These were the stations of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), before God, glory be to Him, sent him as a prophet.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 93, verse 9–11:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him]﴾ ﴿And as for the petitioner, do not repel [him]﴾ ﴿And as for the favor of your Lord, proclaim [it]﴾

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So as for the orphan﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿do not oppress [him]﴾ means: do not wrong him, so that you take away his right, belittling him.

As:

— Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him]﴾: that is, do not wrong [him].

— Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him]﴾, he said: you look down upon him and despise him. And it has been mentioned that in the codex of Abdullah it reads ﴿fa-la takhar﴾ (do not be harsh with him).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And as for the petitioner, do not repel [him]﴾

It means: and as for whoever asks you out of need, do not turn him away; rather, feed him and fulfill his need. ﴿And as for the favor of your Lord, proclaim [it]﴾: that is, mention it.

The people of interpretation have said similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

— Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And as for the favor of your Lord, proclaim [it]﴾, he said: by the prophethood.

— Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Uliyyah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Iyas al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, who said: The Muslims used to consider that among the thanks for blessings is to speak of them.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Duha, and to Allah belongs all praise and thanks.
